when: 2026-08-09, run on the committed tree at checkpoint 6 (b4ba572) and re-run afterwards; the verbatim substitutions were written down in the fixup round of PR #360 (finding F5)
what: Criterion 7 of Issue #358: one mutant per half of the change, not one for the change as a whole. A check that only reddens when the whole edit is reverted proves one half is covered and says nothing about the other.

howToReproduce.runner: .artifacts/mutate-358.py — applies each replacement to one source file, runs the checks, records the summary and the names that went red, and puts the file back in a finally block. It re-runs the checks afterwards, so the last line of its output is the shipped tree.
howToReproduce.whereTheRunnerIs: .artifacts is in .gitignore, so the runner is not in the repository and the record of what was mutated has to be the substitution itself. Independent review of PR #360 reconstructed mutant 2 from a prose description and got the stated result — but it was a reconstruction, and that is finding F5. Every `was` / `became` below is copy-pasteable: replace the one in the named file, run the checks command, put the file back.
howToReproduce.baseline: 10 of 10 green on the shipped tree, run last, after every mutation was put back
howToReproduce.whyThisSuite: the ten checks of PrototypeReturningRaiderTests are the ones that state the four rules. The whole project is green too — 347 of 347, evidence/358-invariants.json — but a mutation pass over a suite that also holds 337 unrelated checks would report noise beside the signal.
howToReproduce.whyAfterTheCommit: a mutation is put back with a write and, if anything goes wrong, with `git checkout --`. On Issue #147 that restore was run against an uncommitted file and took the change with it. The tree was committed first.

mutants.whyNotTheTuningConstant: changing T.returning_raider_wave_gap moves the check as well, because the check reads the same constant. The mutant has to break the rule and not the number, so it is the expression that is edited.

mutants.half: the composition rule — a returning raider takes a place, never adds one
mutants.reading: a returning raider no longer consumes one of the wave's places, so he arrives on top of the wave instead of inside it
